version: Numbers in the SQL cards are live; the commentary text is static and should be re-read after new data is added.

cards.title: 440290 is ~32x 440210 by value and 2.7x 440220
cards.sql: SELECT hs6 AS hsn, COUNT(DISTINCT destination) AS markets, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,1) AS value_m, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments WHERE flow='Import' AND record_type='monthly_aggregate' AND date>='2025-11-01' GROUP BY hs6 ORDER BY value_m DESC
cards.read: Official customs import totals, Nov-25 onward. 440290 is ~$736M and ~1.05M t across the 37 markets with official totals; 440220 ~$269M; 440210 ~$23M. 440210 is a niche inside a very large category.
cards.caveat: Markets covered differ by HSN, so sizes are lower bounds, not market totals.

cards.title: EU official imports 2022-2025: 440290 is flat, 440220 up 58%, 440210 halved
cards.sql: SELECT year, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440290' THEN value_usd END)/1e6,1) AS v440290_m, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440290' AND price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440290' AND price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS price_440290, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440290' AND kg IS NOT NULL THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440290' THEN value_usd END)) AS pct_value_with_weight_440290, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440220' THEN value_usd END)/1e6,1) AS v440220_m, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440220' AND price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440220' AND price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS price_440220, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440210' THEN value_usd END)/1e6,1) AS v440210_m, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440210' AND price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN hs6='440210' AND price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS price_440210 FROM shipments WHERE flow='Import' AND record_type='monthly_aggregate' AND destination IN ('Austria','Belgium','Bulgaria','Croatia','Cyprus','Czech Republic','Denmark','Estonia','Finland','France','Germany','Greece','Hungary','Ireland','Italy','Latvia','Lithuania','Luxembourg','Malta','Netherlands','Poland','Portugal','Romania','Slovakia','Slovenia','Spain','Sweden') AND reporter IN ('Austria','Belgium','Bulgaria','Croatia','Cyprus','Czech Republic','Denmark','Estonia','Finland','France','Germany','Greece','Hungary','Ireland','Italy','Latvia','Lithuania','Luxembourg','Malta','Netherlands','Poland','Portugal','Romania','Slovakia','Slovenia','Spain','Sweden') AND year BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
cards.read: The EU buys ~$490-540M a year of 440290 at a steady $635-665/t: a mature, price-stable market. 440220 grew from $18M to $29M (+58%) at ~$880-930/t. 440210 imports halved in 2025 ($7M against $15-18M before) and its price fell from ~$2,000 to ~$1,400/t.
cards.caveat: EU member-state customs totals, 27 countries. Volza carries no quantity for ~39% of 2024 440290 value (generic UNT unit, zero quantity), so 2024 tonnes are understated: use value and price for that year. 2026 is excluded (partial).

cards.title: EU 440290 demand is seasonal: ~90 kt a month in May-June against ~51 kt in autumn
cards.sql: SELECT substr(month,6,2) AS month_of_year, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)/3/1000,1) AS avg_kt FROM shipments WHERE flow='Import' AND record_type='monthly_aggregate' AND destination IN ('Austria','Belgium','Bulgaria','Croatia','Cyprus','Czech Republic','Denmark','Estonia','Finland','France','Germany','Greece','Hungary','Ireland','Italy','Latvia','Lithuania','Luxembourg','Malta','Netherlands','Poland','Portugal','Romania','Slovakia','Slovenia','Spain','Sweden') AND reporter IN ('Austria','Belgium','Bulgaria','Croatia','Cyprus','Czech Republic','Denmark','Estonia','Finland','France','Germany','Greece','Hungary','Ireland','Italy','Latvia','Lithuania','Luxembourg','Malta','Netherlands','Poland','Portugal','Romania','Slovakia','Slovenia','Spain','Sweden') AND hs6='440290' AND year IN (2022,2023,2025) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cards.read: Average monthly EU imports (2022, 2023, 2025) climb from ~57 kt in January to a peak of ~92 kt in May, stay high through July, then fall to ~51-54 kt from September. This is the BBQ season, so shipments need to land by March to April.
cards.caveat: 2024 is excluded because of the weight gap noted in the trend card. Tonnes are official weights.

cards.title: Who supplies the EU with 440290: Ukraine, Namibia and Cuba lead, Indonesia and Paraguay are shrinking
cards.sql: SELECT origin, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN year=2022 THEN value_usd END)/1e6,1) AS v_2022, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN year=2023 THEN value_usd END)/1e6,1) AS v_2023, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN year=2024 THEN value_usd END)/1e6,1) AS v_2024, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN year=2025 THEN value_usd END)/1e6,1) AS v_2025, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN year IN (2022,2023,2025) THEN tonnes END)/3/1000,0) AS avg_kt_yr FROM shipments WHERE flow='Import' AND record_type='monthly_aggregate' AND destination IN ('Austria','Belgium','Bulgaria','Croatia','Cyprus','Czech Republic','Denmark','Estonia','Finland','France','Germany','Greece','Hungary','Ireland','Italy','Latvia','Lithuania','Luxembourg','Malta','Netherlands','Poland','Portugal','Romania','Slovakia','Slovenia','Spain','Sweden') AND reporter IN ('Austria','Belgium','Bulgaria','Croatia','Cyprus','Czech Republic','Denmark','Estonia','Finland','France','Germany','Greece','Hungary','Ireland','Italy','Latvia','Lithuania','Luxembourg','Malta','Netherlands','Poland','Portugal','Romania','Slovakia','Slovenia','Spain','Sweden') AND hs6='440290' AND year BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 AND origin IS NOT NULL AND origin NOT IN ('Austria','Belgium','Bulgaria','Croatia','Cyprus','Czech Republic','Denmark','Estonia','Finland','France','Germany','Greece','Hungary','Ireland','Italy','Latvia','Lithuania','Luxembourg','Malta','Netherlands','Poland','Portugal','Romania','Slovakia','Slovenia','Spain','Sweden') GROUP BY origin ORDER BY SUM(value_usd) DESC LIMIT 12
cards.read: Extra-EU suppliers by value ($M). Ukraine is steady at ~$75M a year (~115 kt). Namibia has risen to $73M in 2025 (~119 kt), Nigeria to $29M. Indonesia collapsed from $54M in 2022 to ~$24M and Paraguay from $30M to ~$19M. Vietnam is marginal at ~$5M.
cards.caveat: Official country-of-origin data. 2024 tonnage is understated (see trend card), so avg_kt_yr uses 2022, 2023 and 2025 only.

cards.title: 440290: China and Saudi Arabia lead on tonnes, Germany and Korea on value
cards.sql: SELECT destination, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,1) AS value_m, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t, COUNT(*) AS rows_ FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440290' AND flow='Import' AND record_type='monthly_aggregate' AND date>='2025-11-01' AND destination IS NOT NULL GROUP BY destination ORDER BY tonnes DESC LIMIT 16
cards.read: China imports ~192,000 t but at ~$285/t (mostly Myanmar), so only ~$55M. Saudi Arabia ~88,000 t, Germany ~82,000 t, Netherlands ~74,000 t, Japan ~65,000 t, South Korea ~58,000 t. By value Germany (~$66M), South Korea (~$64M), Japan (~$63M) and the Netherlands (~$62M) are level; Korea and Japan pay the most per tonne among the big importers.
cards.caveat: Only the importer markets pulled (see the coverage table in About). UK's official feed starts Jan-2026 (understated). The US has no official totals here, only bill-of-lading rows.

cards.title: What importers pay for 440290: ~$1,100/t in Korea and France, ~$285/t in China
cards.sql: SELECT destination, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN tonnes END)) AS tonnes_priced FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440290' AND flow='Import' AND record_type='monthly_aggregate' AND date>='2025-11-01' AND destination IS NOT NULL GROUP BY destination HAVING tonnes_priced>=5000 ORDER BY avg_price_usd_t DESC
cards.read: Weighted customs value per tonne. South Korea ~$1,113, France ~$1,074, Sweden ~$974, Japan ~$958, Germany ~$813, UK ~$839, Saudi ~$575, Poland ~$566, China ~$285. The spread is mostly product mix: cheap lump charcoal (Paraguay, Myanmar) versus briquettes and sawdust charcoal (Indonesia, Vietnam) versus premium restaurant grade.
cards.caveat: Customs value, not a quote. Rows implying under $50/t were dropped from tonnage as unit errors (318 rows in 440290).

cards.title: Who ships to whom: Paraguay dominates European and Saudi lump charcoal at $175-310/t
cards.sql: SELECT origin || ' > ' || destination AS lane, COUNT(*) AS shipments, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440290' AND record_type='shipment' AND origin IS NOT NULL AND destination IS NOT NULL AND flow IN ('Export','Import') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY tonnes DESC LIMIT 20
cards.read: Named shipments (Nov-25 to Oct-26). Paraguay to UK ~86,000 t at ~$214/t, Paraguay to Germany ~44,000 t at ~$176/t, Indonesia to Saudi ~35,000 t at ~$479/t, Vietnam to Japan ~17,000 t at ~$550/t, Ukraine to Poland/Germany ~$620-860/t. Asian buyers (Japan, Korea, Saudi) are served by Indonesia and Vietnam at $480-730/t.
cards.caveat: Shipment rows cover 18% to 100% of official volume depending on the importer (see the coverage card), so lane totals are a sample. Not additive with the official totals.

cards.title: Named 440290 buyers in the priority markets (Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Saudi, UAE)
cards.sql: SELECT c.name AS company, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT destination) AS destinations, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT origin) AS sourced_from, COUNT(*) AS shipments, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments s JOIN companies c ON c.key = s.buyer_key WHERE hs6='440290' AND record_type='shipment' AND buyer IS NOT NULL AND destination IN ('Japan','South Korea','Taiwan','Saudi Arabia','United Arab Emirates') GROUP BY s.buyer_key ORDER BY tonnes DESC LIMIT 25
cards.read: A ready target list: Idemitsu Kosan (Japan, ~7,500 t from Vietnam), Bijei Muyek and DCM Co. (Korea and Japan, Indonesian briquette charcoal), SS Global Harvest, Takayama, Utex. Saudi buyers (Jealous Devil, Rwazen, Sohol Al Reem, Tal Al Jabia) move 2,000 to 15,000 t each. Large Saudi lots from Paraguay run $170-280/t; Indonesian lots $470-720/t.
cards.caveat: Names are as declared on customs documents, with spelling variants and some trading houses. Verify before outreach.

cards.title: How much of each market's official volume is visible as named shipments
cards.sql: SELECT d.destination, ROUND(d.t) AS named_shipment_t, ROUND(o.t) AS official_t, ROUND(100.0*d.t/o.t) AS pct_visible FROM (SELECT destination, SUM(tonnes) AS t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440290' AND record_type='shipment' AND destination IS NOT NULL GROUP BY destination) d JOIN (SELECT destination, SUM(tonnes) AS t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440290' AND flow='Import' AND record_type='monthly_aggregate' AND date>='2025-11-01' GROUP BY destination) o USING (destination) WHERE o.t > 0 ORDER BY o.t DESC LIMIT 20
cards.read: China 16%, Poland 27%, France 27%, Italy 32%, Netherlands 37%, South Korea 43%, Japan 67%, Germany 70%. Over 100% (Saudi Arabia, UK) means the official feed is incomplete for that country, not that named shipments are wrong: the UK official feed only starts in Jan-2026.
cards.caveat: Use official totals for market size and named shipments for who and at what price. Never add the two: the same trade appears in both.

cards.title: 440210: Japan and South Korea are the volume markets
cards.sql: SELECT destination, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,2) AS value_m, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440210' AND flow='Import' AND date>='2025-11-01' AND destination IS NOT NULL GROUP BY destination ORDER BY value_m DESC LIMIT 12
cards.read: Japan (~$7.4M, ~8,300 t) and South Korea (~$6.5M, ~7,800 t) lead, then Saudi Arabia (~$1.8M). Europe is many small markets, each under $1M.
cards.caveat: Japan, Korea, Saudi and the UK feeds start Jan-2026, so their figures are ~7-8 months, not 12. US coverage is shipment-level only, so it is understated.

cards.title: 440210 supply is a China story
cards.sql: SELECT origin, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,2) AS value_m, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440210' AND flow='Import' AND date>='2025-11-01' AND origin IS NOT NULL GROUP BY origin ORDER BY value_m DESC LIMIT 12
cards.read: China accounts for ~$17M and ~18,400 t of reported bamboo-charcoal imports. Next best (Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Laos) are each ~$1M or less.
cards.caveat: Origin 'Not available' rows are excluded here. Imports only, to avoid double counting with export feeds.

cards.title: 440210 price: ~$700-900/t in bulk Asia, $1,500-2,400/t in small European lots
cards.sql: SELECT destination, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN tonnes END)) AS tonnes_priced FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440210' AND flow='Import' AND date>='2025-11-01' AND destination IS NOT NULL GROUP BY destination HAVING tonnes_priced>=100 ORDER BY avg_price_usd_t DESC LIMIT 14
cards.read: Weighted CIF/customs-value price. Japan ~$890, South Korea ~$840, Saudi ~$670, India ~$770 per tonne. UK, Netherlands, France, Belgium sit at $1,500-2,400 on far smaller volumes, which is likely packed or graded product (BBQ/retail).
cards.caveat: Customs value is not a quote: it includes freight/insurance on CIF and under-declaration is common. Treat as a floor for what a premium product can fetch.

cards.title: Like-for-like 440210 import trend: value roughly halved 2022 to 2025
cards.sql: SELECT year, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,2) AS value_m, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440210' AND flow='Import' AND year BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 AND reporter IN (SELECT reporter FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440210' AND flow='Import' AND year BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 GROUP BY reporter HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT year)=4) GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
cards.read: Restricted to reporters that have data in every year 2022-2025 (European customs feeds, India, plus a few shipment-level feeds such as Pakistan, Vietnam, Uganda), so the coverage artefact is removed. Value fell ~48% and price ~31%. Do not read this as the global market: the growth markets (Japan, Korea, Saudi) are not in the 2022-25 history.
cards.caveat: This is the only fair trend in the data. A naive yearly sum shows a 2026 spike that is purely new reporters being added.

cards.title: 440220: China imports ~62% of tracked value
cards.sql: SELECT destination, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,1) AS value_m, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440220' AND flow='Import' AND date>='2025-11-01' AND destination IS NOT NULL GROUP BY destination ORDER BY value_m DESC LIMIT 10
cards.read: China ~$181M (~214,000 t at ~$850/t), then India, Japan, Sri Lanka, Netherlands, Saudi Arabia. Japan pays ~$1,400/t, about 65% above China: the activated-carbon grade premium.
cards.caveat: China's rows are monthly customs aggregates (no buyer names). Share is of tracked reporters only.

cards.title: 440220 supply: Philippines and Indonesia
cards.sql: SELECT origin, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,1) AS value_m, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440220' AND flow='Import' AND date>='2025-11-01' AND origin IS NOT NULL GROUP BY origin ORDER BY value_m DESC LIMIT 10
cards.read: Philippines ~$150M, Indonesia ~$84M, then Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand. Nigeria prices at ~$300/t, a clear outlier: cheap feedstock exists but its quality is unknown.
cards.caveat: Prices here are the customs value, mixing grades.

cards.title: Biggest named importers across all three HSNs (by shipments)
cards.sql: SELECT c.name AS company, COUNT(*) AS shipments, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,2) AS value_m, COUNT(DISTINCT destination) AS countries, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT destination) AS importing_countries, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT hs6) AS hsn FROM shipments s JOIN companies c ON c.key = s.buyer_key WHERE s.buyer_key IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.buyer_key ORDER BY shipments DESC LIMIT 25
cards.read: Lump and BBQ charcoal distributors dominate by shipment count: Big K Products (UK, ~74,000 t, sourced from Paraguay, Indonesia and Namibia), Gryfskand (Polish, shipping into Germany, Poland and Bulgaria), Holzkohlewerk Lüneburg (Germany, ~35,000 t) and RJJ Product of Import (Spain, ~17,000 t). In the priority Asian markets the largest are Bijei Muyek, Hana Trading and DSP (South Korea) and Takayama (Japan). DHG Vertriebs ranks sixth by shipments but is a five-country trader with little tonnage per shipment.
cards.caveat: Named buyers exist only on shipment-level rows (about 60% of records). Rank by shipments, since tonnes are blank on lines without a KGS weight. Spelling variants are merged, not legal entities: group companies may still appear separately.

cards.title: Importers buying more than one HSN
cards.sql: SELECT c.name AS company, COUNT(DISTINCT hs6) AS hsn_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT hs6) AS hsn, COUNT(*) AS shipments, COUNT(DISTINCT destination) AS countries, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes FROM shipments s JOIN companies c ON c.key = s.buyer_key WHERE s.buyer_key IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.buyer_key HAVING hsn_count >= 2 ORDER BY shipments DESC LIMIT 25
cards.read: Buyers spanning HSNs are mostly Asian traders and activated-carbon users: Hebei Yulunsi (China, all three HSNs, ~7,200 t), SS Global Harvest (Malaysia, selling into Japan, Saudi Arabia and the UAE), Osaka Gas Chemicals (Japan, 440220 and 440290, ~8,400 t), DCM, Taur Young and Huge Mountain. These are the accounts that would take a mixed offer of shell, wood and bamboo-derived products.
cards.caveat: A company appearing under several HSNs may be a trader or distributor rather than an end user.

cards.title: Named buyers of 440220 are activated-carbon makers
cards.sql: SELECT c.name AS company, COUNT(*) AS shipments, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,2) AS value_m, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT destination) AS destinations FROM shipments s JOIN companies c ON c.key = s.buyer_key WHERE hs6='440220' AND record_type='shipment' AND buyer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.buyer_key ORDER BY tonnes DESC LIMIT 15
cards.read: Xiamen Phisoul, Jacobi Carbons Lanka, Tianjin Brilliant, Osaka Gas Chemicals, Kuraray and Chang Zhou Qi Di are the real activated-carbon converters. Also visible: Shomoukh Al Rayed (Saudi Arabia, ~5,400 t) and United Carbon Solutions (India, ~4,600 t), a direct Indian buyer. Guess: some would test bamboo char as an alternative feedstock.
cards.caveat: Names come mostly from export-side shipment feeds (Philippines, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Indonesia). Buyers inside China's official totals are anonymous. Variants of one company are merged.

cards.title: Named 440210 buyers are thin and small
cards.sql: SELECT c.name AS company, COUNT(*) AS shipments, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,2) AS value_m, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT destination) AS destinations FROM shipments s JOIN companies c ON c.key = s.buyer_key WHERE hs6='440210' AND record_type='shipment' AND buyer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.buyer_key ORDER BY tonnes DESC, shipments DESC LIMIT 15
cards.read: Only ~950 of 10,400 bamboo records are shipment-level, and the biggest named buyer with a usable weight moved 128 t in total. US bill-of-lading rows name importers (B&B Charcoal, EB Express Provisions, Dancoal, Susshi) but carry no usable tonnage, and many are Brazilian/Colombian wood charcoal declared under this code. This data will not build a bamboo buyer list; use it for market and price sizing, then buy contact data elsewhere.
cards.caveat: Many named buyers are traders (Pakistan, Vietnam, Uganda), not end users. HS 440210 is also misused for general charcoal.

cards.title: Data quality: what each record type can and cannot answer
cards.sql: SELECT record_type, COUNT(*) AS rows, SUM(buyer IS NOT NULL) AS with_buyer, SUM(kg IS NOT NULL) AS with_weight, SUM(price_ok) AS priced_ok, ROUND(100.0*SUM(price_ok)/COUNT(*)) AS pct_priced, ROUND(SUM(value_usd)/1e6,1) AS value_m FROM shipments GROUP BY record_type
cards.read: monthly_aggregate rows (customs totals per country pair) carry ~70% of value but no names. shipment rows carry names but ~30%. directory rows are a one-off listing. Aggregates and shipments overlap for the same trade: never add them.
cards.caveat: Rows with units other than KGS (pieces, bags) have no tonnage or price. Prices outside $50-15,000/t are flagged price_ok=0; implied prices under $50/t also lose their tonnage (source unit errors, e.g. India-Bhutan rows reporting 365,000 t). US bill-of-lading rows have no value and no usable weight.

cards.title: Coverage map: which reporter has data from when (read before trusting any trend)
cards.sql: SELECT reporter, flow, hs6, MIN(month) AS first_month, MAX(month) AS last_month, COUNT(*) AS rows FROM shipments WHERE reporter IS NOT NULL GROUP BY reporter, flow, hs6 ORDER BY rows DESC LIMIT 60
cards.read: European feeds run Nov-2021 to Jul-2026. China imports start 2025; Japan, Korea, Saudi, UK, Australia start Jan-2026. HS 440290 was pulled for Nov-2025 to Oct-2026 only, for 28 importer markets.
cards.caveat: Import and Export feeds of the same trade overlap: a Philippines export to China is also a China import. Never add the two flows.

cards.title: 440220 import price by month (weighted, tracked reporters)
cards.sql: SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN value_usd END)/SUM(CASE WHEN price_ok THEN kg END)*1000) AS avg_price_usd_t, ROUND(SUM(tonnes)) AS tonnes FROM shipments WHERE hs6='440220' AND flow='Import' AND month>='2025-11' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
cards.read: A twelve-month view of the AC feedstock price. Check the tonnes column: thin months are noisy.
cards.caveat: Only 12 months of shell charcoal were pulled; no multi-year trend is possible yet.
